name: Medspa team kickoff playbook for 90-day program
summary:
**Conversation Overview**

The user requested creation of a comprehensive Team Kickoff Playbook for medspa owners to use during staff meetings for their 90-day growth program. Claude analyzed multiple uploaded deliverables including Package & Upsell Architecture Framework, Ultimate MedSpa Membership Playbook, Partnership & Collaboration Framework, and MedSpa Creative Asset Guide to extract staff-specific action items. The user emphasized that the playbook should focus solely on what the team needs to do, not what the agency handles, and should reference the detailed playbooks rather than duplicate content.

Claude initially created a detailed 11-section playbook covering program overview, weekly action items, package implementation, membership launch, partnership building, client experience enhancement, creative asset collection, bi-weekly call preparation, celebration event planning, and quick reference checklists. However, the user requested a much simpler, one-page format with less detail. Claude then created a streamlined "Quick Start Guide" that provides week-by-week checklists while referencing eight comprehensive playbooks: Package & Upsell Architecture Framework, Ultimate MedSpa Membership Playbook, Partnership & Collaboration Framework, Complete Lifetime Value Sales Playbook, Reputation Engine Playbook, Laser ROI Playbook, 90-Day Celebration Event Playbook, and MedSpa Creative Asset Guide.

The user made several specific refinements including removing certain action items that AI tools would handle (like responding to ad leads within 5 minutes), clarifying the division between AI automation and staff responsibilities, moving celebration event planning tasks to earlier weeks, and adding Slack support with 48-hour response time. The final deliverable is a scannable one-page guide with clear weekly milestones, target metrics, and quick reference sections that teams can use for daily progress tracking while diving into detailed playbooks for execution guidance.

**Tool Knowledge**

Claude used document processing tools to extract content from multiple file formats. When working with DOCX files, the pandoc command successfully converted Word documents to readable text format using the syntax "pandoc [filepath] -o [output.txt]". For PDF files, the pdftotext command extracted content effectively with "pdftotext [filepath] [output.txt]". The view tool with specific range parameters like "view_range":[1, 200] allowed efficient scanning of large extracted text files to identify relevant sections without overwhelming output. When creating structured documents, Claude found that using consistent formatting with ASCII borders and clear section dividers improved readability in plain text format. The str_replace tool proved essential for iterative document refinement, allowing precise modifications to specific sections while preserving the overall document structure and formatting.

     5	---
     6	
     7	# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis
     8	
     9	## Overview
    10	
    11	A .docx file is a ZIP archive containing XML files.
    12	
    13	## Quick Reference
    14	
    15	| Task | Approach |
    16	|------|----------|
    17	| Read/analyze content | `pandoc` or unpack for raw XML |
    18	| Create new document | Use `docx-js` - see Creating New Documents below |
    19	| Edit existing document | Unpack → edit XML → repack - see Editing Existing Documents below |
    20	
    21	### Converting .doc to .docx
    22	
    23	Legacy `.doc` files must be converted before editing:
    24	
    25	```bash
    26	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx document.doc
    27	```
    28	
    29	### Reading Content
    30	
    31	```bash
    32	# Text extraction with tracked changes
    33	pandoc --track-changes=all document.docx -o output.md
    34	
    35	# Raw XML access
    36	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
    37	```
    38	
    39	### Converting to Images
    40	
    41	```bash
    42	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf document.docx
    43	pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 document.pdf page
    44	```
    45	
    46	### Accepting Tracked Changes
    47	
    48	To produce a clean document with all tracked changes accepted (requires LibreOffice):
    49	
    50	```bash
    51	python scripts/accept_changes.py input.docx output.docx
    52	```
    53	
    54	---
    55	
    56	## Creating New Documents
    57	
    58	Generate .docx files with JavaScript, then validate. Install: `npm install -g docx`
    59	
    60	### Setup
    61	```javascript
    62	const { Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, Table, TableRow, TableCell, ImageRun,
    63	        Header, Footer, AlignmentType, PageOrientation, LevelFormat, ExternalHyperlink,
    64	        TableOfContents, HeadingLevel, BorderStyle, WidthType, ShadingType,
    65	        VerticalAlign, PageNumber, PageBreak } = require('docx');
    66	
    67	const doc = new Document({ sections: [{ children: [/* content */] }] });
    68	Packer.toBuffer(doc).then(buffer => fs.writeFileSync("doc.docx", buffer));
    69	```
    70	
    71	### Validation
    72	After creating the file, validate it. If validation fails, unpack, fix the XML, and repack.
    73	```bash
    74	python scripts/office/validate.py doc.docx
    75	```
    76	
    77	### Page Size
    78	
    79	```javascript
    80	// CRITICAL: docx-js defaults to A4, not US Letter
    81	// Always set page size explicitly for consistent results
    82	sections: [{
    83	  properties: {
    84	    page: {
    85	      size: {
    86	        width: 12240,   // 8.5 inches in DXA
    87	        height: 15840   // 11 inches in DXA
    88	      },
    89	      margin: { top: 1440, right: 1440, bottom: 1440, left: 1440 } // 1 inch margins
    90	    }
    91	  },
    92	  children: [/* content */]
    93	}]
    94	```
    95	
    96	**Common page sizes (DXA units, 1440 DXA = 1 inch):**
    97	
    98	| Paper | Width | Height | Content Width (1" margins) |
    99	|-------|-------|--------|---------------------------|
   100	| US Letter | 12,240 | 15,840 | 9,360 |
   101	| A4 (default) | 11,906 | 16,838 | 9,026 |
   102	
   103	**Landscape orientation:** docx-js swaps width/height internally, so pass portrait dimensions and let it handle the swap:
   104	```javascript
   105	size: {
   106	  width: 12240,   // Pass SHORT edge as width
   107	  height: 15840,  // Pass LONG edge as height
   108	  orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE  // docx-js swaps them in the XML
   109	},
   110	// Content width = 15840 - left margin - right margin (uses the long edge)
   111	```
   112	
   113	### Styles (Override Built-in Headings)
   114	
   115	Use Arial as the default font (universally supported). Keep titles black for readability.
   116	
   117	```javascript
   118	const doc = new Document({
   119	  styles: {
   120	    default: { document: { run: { font: "Arial", size: 24 } } }, // 12pt default
   121	    paragraphStyles: [
   122	      // IMPORTANT: Use exact IDs to override built-in styles
   123	      { id: "Heading1", name: "Heading 1", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   124	        run: { size: 32, bold: true, font: "Arial" },
   125	        paragraph: { spacing: { before: 240, after: 240 }, outlineLevel: 0 } }, // outlineLevel required for TOC
   126	      { id: "Heading2", name: "Heading 2", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   127	        run: { size: 28, bold: true, font: "Arial" },
   128	        paragraph: { spacing: { before: 180, after: 180 }, outlineLevel: 1 } },
   129	    ]
   130	  },
   131	  sections: [{
   132	    children: [
   133	      new Paragraph({ heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, children: [new TextRun("Title")] }),
   134	    ]
   135	  }]
   136	});
   137	```
   138	
   139	### Lists (NEVER use unicode bullets)
   140	
   141	```javascript
   142	// ❌ WRONG - never manually insert bullet characters
   143	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("• Item")] })  // BAD
   144	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("\u2022 Item")] })  // BAD
   145	
   146	// ✅ CORRECT - use numbering config with LevelFormat.BULLET
   147	const doc = new Document({
   148	  numbering: {
   149	    config: [
   150	      { reference: "bullets",
   151	        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.BULLET, text: "•", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,
   152	          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },
   153	      { reference: "numbers",
   154	        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.DECIMAL, text: "%1.", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,
   155	          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },
   156	    ]
   157	  },
   158	  sections: [{
   159	    children: [
   160	      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: "bullets", level: 0 },
   161	        children: [new TextRun("Bullet item")] }),
   162	      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: "numbers", level: 0 },
   163	        children: [new TextRun("Numbered item")] }),
   164	    ]
   165	  }]
   166	});
   167	
   168	// ⚠️ Each reference creates INDEPENDENT numbering
   169	// Same reference = continues (1,2,3 then 4,5,6)
   170	// Different reference = restarts (1,2,3 then 1,2,3)
   171	```
   172	
   173	### Tables
   174	
   175	**CRITICAL: Tables need dual widths** - set both `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on each cell. Without both, tables render incorrectly on some platforms.
   176	
   177	```javascript
   178	// CRITICAL: Always set table width for consistent rendering
   179	// CRITICAL: Use ShadingType.CLEAR (not SOLID) to prevent black backgrounds
   180	const border = { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 1, color: "CCCCCC" };
   181	const borders = { top: border, bottom: border, left: border, right: border };
   182	
   183	new Table({
   184	  width: { size: 9360, type: WidthType.DXA }, // Always use DXA (percentages break in Google Docs)
   185	  columnWidths: [4680, 4680], // Must sum to table width (DXA: 1440 = 1 inch)
   186	  rows: [
   187	    new TableRow({
   188	      children: [
   189	        new TableCell({
   190	          borders,
   191	          width: { size: 4680, type: WidthType.DXA }, // Also set on each cell
   192	          shading: { fill: "D5E8F0", type: ShadingType.CLEAR }, // CLEAR not SOLID
   193	          margins: { top: 80, bottom: 80, left: 120, right: 120 }, // Cell padding (internal, not added to width)
   194	          children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("Cell")] })]
   195	        })
   196	      ]
   197	    })
   198	  ]
   199	})
   200	```
   201	
   202	**Table width calculation:**
   203	
   204	Always use `WidthType.DXA` — `WidthType.PERCENTAGE` breaks in Google Docs.
   205	
   206	```javascript
   207	// Table width = sum of columnWidths = content width
   208	// US Letter with 1" margins: 12240 - 2880 = 9360 DXA
   209	width: { size: 9360, type: WidthType.DXA },
   210	columnWidths: [7000, 2360]  // Must sum to table width
   211	```
   212	
   213	**Width rules:**
   214	- **Always use `WidthType.DXA`** — never `WidthType.PERCENTAGE` (incompatible with Google Docs)
   215	- Table width must equal the sum of `columnWidths`
   216	- Cell `width` must match corresponding `columnWidth`
   217	- Cell `margins` are internal padding - they reduce content area, not add to cell width
   218	- For full-width tables: use content width (page width minus left and right margins)
   219	
   220	### Images
	< truncated lines 221-262 >
   263	      children: [new TextRun("Page "), new TextRun({ children: [PageNumber.CURRENT] })]
   264	    })] })
   265	  },
   266	  children: [/* content */]
   267	}]
   268	```
   269	
   270	### Critical Rules for docx-js
   271	
   272	- **Set page size explicitly** - docx-js defaults to A4; use US Letter (12240 x 15840 DXA) for US documents
   273	- **Landscape: pass portrait dimensions** - docx-js swaps width/height internally; pass short edge as `width`, long edge as `height`, and set `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE`
   274	- **Never use `\n`** - use separate Paragraph elements
   275	- **Never use unicode bullets** - use `LevelFormat.BULLET` with numbering config
   276	- **PageBreak must be in Paragraph** - standalone creates invalid XML
   277	- **ImageRun requires `type`** - always specify png/jpg/etc
   278	- **Always set table `width` with DXA** - never use `WidthType.PERCENTAGE` (breaks in Google Docs)
   279	- **Tables need dual widths** - `columnWidths` array AND cell `width`, both must match
   280	- **Table width = sum of columnWidths** - for DXA, ensure they add up exactly
   281	- **Always add cell margins** - use `margins: { top: 80, bottom: 80, left: 120, right: 120 }` for readable padding
   282	- **Use `ShadingType.CLEAR`** - never SOLID for table shading
   283	- **TOC requires HeadingLevel only** - no custom styles on heading paragraphs
   284	- **Override built-in styles** - use exact IDs: "Heading1", "Heading2", etc.
   285	- **Include `outlineLevel`** - required for TOC (0 for H1, 1 for H2, etc.)
   286	
   287	---
   288	
   289	## Editing Existing Documents
   290	
   291	**Follow all 3 steps in order.**
   292	
   293	### Step 1: Unpack
   294	```bash
   295	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
   296	```
   297	Extracts XML, pretty-prints, merges adjacent runs, and converts smart quotes to XML entities (`“` etc.) so they survive editing. Use `--merge-runs false` to skip run merging.
   298	
   299	### Step 2: Edit XML
   300	
   301	Edit files in `unpacked/word/`. See XML Reference below for patterns.
   302	
   303	**Use "Claude" as the author** for tracked changes and comments, unless the user explicitly requests use of a different name.
   304	
   305	**Use the Edit tool directly for string replacement. Do not write Python scripts.** Scripts introduce unnecessary complexity. The Edit tool shows exactly what is being replaced.
   306	
   307	**CRITICAL: Use smart quotes for new content.** When adding text with apostrophes or quotes, use XML entities to produce smart quotes:
   308	```xml
   309	<!-- Use these entities for professional typography -->
   310	<w:t>Here’s a quote: “Hello”</w:t>
   311	```
   312	| Entity | Character |
   313	|--------|-----------|
   314	| `‘` | ‘ (left single) |
   315	| `’` | ’ (right single / apostrophe) |
   316	| `“` | “ (left double) |
   317	| `”` | ” (right double) |
   318	
   319	**Adding comments:** Use `comment.py` to handle boilerplate across multiple XML files (text must be pre-escaped XML):
   320	```bash
   321	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Comment text with & and ’"
   322	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 1 "Reply text" --parent 0  # reply to comment 0
   323	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Text" --author "Custom Author"  # custom author name
   324	```
   325	Then add markers to document.xml (see Comments in XML Reference).
   326	
   327	### Step 3: Pack
   328	```bash
   329	python scripts/office/pack.py unpacked/ output.docx --original document.docx
   330	```
   331	Validates with auto-repair, condenses XML, and creates DOCX. Use `--validate false` to skip.
   332	
   333	**Auto-repair will fix:**
   334	- `durableId` >= 0x7FFFFFFF (regenerates valid ID)
   335	- Missing `xml:space="preserve"` on `<w:t>` with whitespace
   336	
   337	**Auto-repair won't fix:**
   338	- Malformed XML, invalid element nesting, missing relationships, schema violations
   339	
   340	### Common Pitfalls
   341	
   342	- **Replace entire `<w:r>` elements**: When adding tracked changes, replace the whole `<w:r>...</w:r>` block with `<w:del>...<w:ins>...` as siblings. Don't inject tracked change tags inside a run.
   343	- **Preserve `<w:rPr>` formatting**: Copy the original run's `<w:rPr>` block into your tracked change runs to maintain bold, font size, etc.
   344	
   345	---
   346	
   347	## XML Reference
   348	
   349	### Schema Compliance
   350	
   351	- **Element order in `<w:pPr>`**: `<w:pStyle>`, `<w:numPr>`, `<w:spacing>`, `<w:ind>`, `<w:jc>`, `<w:rPr>` last
   352	- **Whitespace**: Add `xml:space="preserve"` to `<w:t>` with leading/trailing spaces
   353	- **RSIDs**: Must be 8-digit hex (e.g., `00AB1234`)
   354	
   355	### Tracked Changes
   356	
   357	**Insertion:**
   358	```xml
   359	<w:ins w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   360	  <w:r><w:t>inserted text</w:t></w:r>
   361	</w:ins>
   362	```
   363	
   364	**Deletion:**
   365	```xml
   366	<w:del w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   367	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>
   368	</w:del>
   369	```
   370	
   371	**Inside `<w:del>`**: Use `<w:delText>` instead of `<w:t>`, and `<w:delInstrText>` instead of `<w:instrText>`.
   372	
   373	**Minimal edits** - only mark what changes:
   374	```xml
   375	<!-- Change "30 days" to "60 days" -->
   376	<w:r><w:t>The term is </w:t></w:r>
   377	<w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="...">
   378	  <w:r><w:delText>30</w:delText></w:r>
   379	</w:del>
   380	<w:ins w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="...">
   381	  <w:r><w:t>60</w:t></w:r>
   382	</w:ins>
   383	<w:r><w:t> days.</w:t></w:r>
   384	```
   385	
   386	**Deleting entire paragraphs/list items** - when removing ALL content from a paragraph, also mark the paragraph mark as deleted so it merges with the next paragraph. Add `<w:del/>` inside `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`:
   387	```xml
   388	<w:p>
   389	  <w:pPr>
   390	    <w:numPr>...</w:numPr>  <!-- list numbering if present -->
   391	    <w:rPr>
   392	      <w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
   393	    </w:rPr>
   394	  </w:pPr>
   395	  <w:del w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   396	    <w:r><w:delText>Entire paragraph content being deleted...</w:delText></w:r>
   397	  </w:del>
   398	</w:p>
   399	```
   400	Without the `<w:del/>` in `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`, accepting changes leaves an empty paragraph/list item.
   401	
   402	**Rejecting another author's insertion** - nest deletion inside their insertion:
   403	```xml
   404	<w:ins w:author="Jane" w:id="5">
   405	  <w:del w:author="Claude" w:id="10">
   406	    <w:r><w:delText>their inserted text</w:delText></w:r>
   407	  </w:del>
   408	</w:ins>
   409	```
   410	
   411	**Restoring another author's deletion** - add insertion after (don't modify their deletion):
   412	```xml
   413	<w:del w:author="Jane" w:id="5">
   414	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>
   415	</w:del>
   416	<w:ins w:author="Claude" w:id="10">
   417	  <w:r><w:t>deleted text</w:t></w:r>
   418	</w:ins>
   419	```
   420	
   421	### Comments
   422	
   423	After running `comment.py` (see Step 2), add markers to document.xml. For replies, use `--parent` flag and nest markers inside the parent's.
   424	
   425	**CRITICAL: `<w:commentRangeStart>` and `<w:commentRangeEnd>` are siblings of `<w:r>`, never inside `<w:r>`.**
   426	
   427	```xml
   428	<!-- Comment markers are direct children of w:p, never inside w:r -->

     7	# PDF Processing Guide
     8	
     9	## Overview
    10	
    11	This guide covers essential PDF processing operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features, JavaScript libraries, and detailed examples, see REFERENCE.md. If you need to fill out a PDF form, read FORMS.md and follow its instructions.
    12	
    13	## Quick Start
    14	
    15	```python
    16	from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter
    17	
    18	# Read a PDF
    19	reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
    20	print(f"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}")
    21	
    22	# Extract text
    23	text = ""
    24	for page in reader.pages:
    25	    text += page.extract_text()
    26	```
    27	
    28	## Python Libraries
    29	
    30	### pypdf - Basic Operations
    31	
    32	#### Merge PDFs
    33	```python
    34	from pypdf import PdfWriter, PdfReader
    35	
    36	writer = PdfWriter()
    37	for pdf_file in ["doc1.pdf", "doc2.pdf", "doc3.pdf"]:
    38	    reader = PdfReader(pdf_file)
    39	    for page in reader.pages:
    40	        writer.add_page(page)
    41	
    42	with open("merged.pdf", "wb") as output:
    43	    writer.write(output)
    44	```
    45	
    46	#### Split PDF
    47	```python
    48	reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
    49	for i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
    50	    writer = PdfWriter()
    51	    writer.add_page(page)
    52	    with open(f"page_{i+1}.pdf", "wb") as output:
    53	        writer.write(output)
    54	```
    55	
    56	#### Extract Metadata
    57	```python
    58	reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
    59	meta = reader.metadata
    60	print(f"Title: {meta.title}")
    61	print(f"Author: {meta.author}")
    62	print(f"Subject: {meta.subject}")
    63	print(f"Creator: {meta.creator}")
    64	```
    65	
    66	#### Rotate Pages
    67	```python
    68	reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
    69	writer = PdfWriter()
    70	
    71	page = reader.pages[0]
    72	page.rotate(90)  # Rotate 90 degrees clockwise
    73	writer.add_page(page)
    74	
    75	with open("rotated.pdf", "wb") as output:
    76	    writer.write(output)
    77	```
    78	
    79	### pdfplumber - Text and Table Extraction
    80	
    81	#### Extract Text with Layout
    82	```python
    83	import pdfplumber
    84	
    85	with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    86	    for page in pdf.pages:
    87	        text = page.extract_text()
    88	        print(text)
    89	```
    90	
    91	#### Extract Tables
    92	```python
    93	with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    94	    for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):
    95	        tables = page.extract_tables()
    96	        for j, table in enumerate(tables):
    97	            print(f"Table {j+1} on page {i+1}:")
    98	            for row in table:
    99	                print(row)
   100	```
   101	
   102	#### Advanced Table Extraction
   103	```python
   104	import pandas as pd
   105	
   106	with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
   107	    all_tables = []
   108	    for page in pdf.pages:
   109	        tables = page.extract_tables()
   110	        for table in tables:
   111	            if table:  # Check if table is not empty
   112	                df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])
   113	                all_tables.append(df)
   114	
   115	# Combine all tables
   116	if all_tables:
   117	    combined_df = pd.concat(all_tables, ignore_index=True)
   118	    combined_df.to_excel("extracted_tables.xlsx", index=False)
   119	```

   121	### reportlab - Create PDFs
   122	
   123	#### Basic PDF Creation
   124	```python
   125	from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
   126	from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas
   127	
   128	c = canvas.Canvas("hello.pdf", pagesize=letter)
   129	width, height = letter
   130	
   131	# Add text
   132	c.drawString(100, height - 100, "Hello World!")
   133	c.drawString(100, height - 120, "This is a PDF created with reportlab")
   134	
   135	# Add a line
   136	c.line(100, height - 140, 400, height - 140)
   137	
   138	# Save
   139	c.save()
   140	```
   141	
   142	#### Create PDF with Multiple Pages
   143	```python
   144	from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
   145	from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak
   146	from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet
   147	
   148	doc = SimpleDocTemplate("report.pdf", pagesize=letter)
   149	styles = getSampleStyleSheet()
   150	story = []
   151	
   152	# Add content
   153	title = Paragraph("Report Title", styles['Title'])
   154	story.append(title)
   155	story.append(Spacer(1, 12))
   156	
   157	body = Paragraph("This is the body of the report. " * 20, styles['Normal'])
   158	story.append(body)
   159	story.append(PageBreak())
   160	
   161	# Page 2
   162	story.append(Paragraph("Page 2", styles['Heading1']))
   163	story.append(Paragraph("Content for page 2", styles['Normal']))
   164	
   165	# Build PDF
   166	doc.build(story)
   167	```
   168	
   169	#### Subscripts and Superscripts
   170	
   171	**IMPORTANT**: Never use Unicode subscript/superscript characters (₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉, ⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹) in ReportLab PDFs. The built-in fonts do not include these glyphs, causing them to render as solid black boxes.
   172	
   173	Instead, use ReportLab's XML markup tags in Paragraph objects:
   174	```python
   175	from reportlab.platypus import Paragraph
   176	from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet
   177	
   178	styles = getSampleStyleSheet()
   179	
   180	# Subscripts: use <sub> tag
   181	chemical = Paragraph("H<sub>2</sub>O", styles['Normal'])
   182	
   183	# Superscripts: use <super> tag
   184	squared = Paragraph("x<super>2</super> + y<super>2</super>", styles['Normal'])
   185	```
   186	
   187	For canvas-drawn text (not Paragraph objects), manually adjust font the size and position rather than using Unicode subscripts/superscripts.
   188	
   189	## Command-Line Tools
   190	
   191	### pdftotext (poppler-utils)
   192	```bash
   193	# Extract text
   194	pdftotext input.pdf output.txt
   195	
   196	# Extract text preserving layout
   197	pdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt
   198	
   199	# Extract specific pages
   200	pdftotext -f 1 -l 5 input.pdf output.txt  # Pages 1-5
   201	```
   202	
   203	### qpdf
   204	```bash
   205	# Merge PDFs
   206	qpdf --empty --pages file1.pdf file2.pdf -- merged.pdf
   207	
   208	# Split pages
   209	qpdf input.pdf --pages . 1-5 -- pages1-5.pdf
   210	qpdf input.pdf --pages . 6-10 -- pages6-10.pdf
   211	
   212	# Rotate pages
   213	qpdf input.pdf output.pdf --rotate=+90:1  # Rotate page 1 by 90 degrees
   214	
   215	# Remove password
   216	qpdf --password=mypassword --decrypt encrypted.pdf decrypted.pdf
   217	```
   218	
   219	### pdftk (if available)
   220	```bash
   221	# Merge
   222	pdftk file1.pdf file2.pdf cat output merged.pdf
   223	
   224	# Split
   225	pdftk input.pdf burst
   226	
   227	# Rotate
   228	pdftk input.pdf rotate 1east output rotated.pdf
   229	```
   230	
   231	## Common Tasks
   232	
   233	### Extract Text from Scanned PDFs
   234	```python
   235	# Requires: pip install pytesseract pdf2image
   236	import pytesseract
   237	from pdf2image import convert_from_path
   238	
   239	# Convert PDF to images
   240	images = convert_from_path('scanned.pdf')
   241	
   242	# OCR each page
   243	text = ""
   244	for i, image in enumerate(images):
   245	    text += f"Page {i+1}:\n"
   246	    text += pytesseract.image_to_string(image)
   247	    text += "\n\n"
   248	
   249	print(text)
   250	```
   251	
   252	### Add Watermark
   253	```python
   254	from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter
   255	
   256	# Create watermark (or load existing)
   257	watermark = PdfReader("watermark.pdf").pages[0]
   258	
   259	# Apply to all pages
   260	reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
   261	writer = PdfWriter()
   262	
   263	for page in reader.pages:
   264	    page.merge_page(watermark)
   265	    writer.add_page(page)
   266	
   267	with open("watermarked.pdf", "wb") as output:
   268	    writer.write(output)
   269	```
   270	
   271	### Extract Images
   272	```bash
   273	# Using pdfimages (poppler-utils)
   274	pdfimages -j input.pdf output_prefix
   275	
   276	# This extracts all images as output_prefix-000.jpg, output_prefix-001.jpg, etc.
   277	```
   278	
   279	### Password Protection
   280	```python
   281	from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter
   282	
   283	reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
   284	writer = PdfWriter()
   285	
   286	for page in reader.pages:
   287	    writer.add_page(page)
   288	
   289	# Add password
   290	writer.encrypt("userpassword", "ownerpassword")
   291	
   292	with open("encrypted.pdf", "wb") as output:
   293	    writer.write(output)
   294	```
   295	
   296	## Quick Reference
   297	
   298	| Task | Best Tool | Command/Code |
   299	|------|-----------|--------------|
   300	| Merge PDFs | pypdf | `writer.add_page(page)` |
   301	| Split PDFs | pypdf | One page per file |
   302	| Extract text | pdfplumber | `page.extract_text()` |
   303	| Extract tables | pdfplumber | `page.extract_tables()` |
   304	| Create PDFs | reportlab | Canvas or Platypus |
   305	| Command line merge | qpdf | `qpdf --empty --pages ...` |
   306	| OCR scanned PDFs | pytesseract | Convert to image first |
   307	| Fill PDF forms | pdf-lib or pypdf (see FORMS.md) | See FORMS.md |

{"language": "plaintext", "code": "THE ULTIMATE MEDSPA MEMBERSHIP PLAYBOOK
Transform Your MedSpa Into a Predictable Revenue Machine
A Complete Implementation System for Building High-LTV, No-Brainer Memberships That Convert

TABLE OF CONTENTS
1. Executive Summary: Why This Matters Now
2. The Industry Landscape: What's Working in 2025
3. Membership Psychology: The Science of Commitment
4. The Tier Architecture System
5. Pricing Engineering: The Value Equation
6. Benefit Stacking Framework
7. Retention Mechanisms That Work
8. Launch Strategy Playbook
9. Real-World Success Stories
10. Implementation Timeline
11. ChatGPT Customization Template
12. Performance Tracking Dashboard

SECTION 1: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY {#section-1}
The State of MedSpa Memberships in 2025
Critical Industry Data:
85% of medspas now offer membership programs (up from 61% in 2023)
24% increase in membership sales year-over-year
Members visit 2.9x more frequently than non-members
Members spend 35% more per visit than non-members
Membership programs now contribute 14-30% of total medspa revenue
Well-structured programs can shorten payback period from 36 to 24 months

 The Bottom Line: Memberships aren't optional anymore—they're the foundation of sustainable medspa
growth. But most medspas leave 40-60% of potential revenue on the table with poorly designed programs.
What Makes This Playbook Different
This isn't theory. Every strategy is based on:
Real franchise data from top performers (Dermani, Vitalyc, VIO Med Spa)
Proven retention mechanics from behavioral economics
Actual LTV calculations from 800+ member bases
Implementation timelines tested across 27+ locations

SECTION 2: THE INDUSTRY LANDSCAPE {#section-2}
What the Top Performers Are Doing
Case Study 1: Dermani MEDSPA
The Model: Affordable, high-volume membership approach
Scale: 27 locations, TOP 50 Allergan account in US
Key Strategy: Tiered memberships ($99-$249/month) focusing on Botox/laser volume
Result: Stabilized revenue, 27% of new clients from referrals
Differentiator: Bulk purchasing power creates 10% lower COGS on injectables
What They Do Right:
Membership fees offset seasonality
120+ hours franchisee training on conversion tactics
Centralized CRM for seamless member management
Tech imaging for personalized consultation upsells

Case Study 2: Vitalyc MedSpa
The Model: Premium positioning with lifestyle integration
Scale: Multiple TX locations, aggressive expansion (25 locations by 2026)
Key Strategy: Gold ($99/mo) and Black ($180/mo) tiers with clear value proposition
Result: Celebrity clientele, premium brand perception

 Differentiator: Uber-like scheduling platform, 12-month commitment required
What They Do Right:
Freeze options (up to 3 months/year after 4 months)
Member-only exclusive events throughout year
15% discount on all services including Botox/fillers
No penalty cancellation when terms are met

Case Study 3: VIO Med Spa
The Model: Multi-tier franchise with referral stacking
Scale: National franchise presence
Key Strategy: Silver, Gold, Platinum ($129-$249/month)
Result: 27% of new clients from member referrals
Differentiator: $50 credit per friend referred
What They Do Right:
Cross-brand partnerships (Glow Sauna Studios) for lifestyle ecosystem
Pre-launch membership sales ($80k-$120k before opening)
Service mix optimization (injectables vs. energy-based)
Systematic 6-8 week pre-opening campaign

Industry Benchmarks You Need to Know
Revenue Metrics:
Average ticket size (2024): $454 (down from $500 in 2023)
Package revenue: 29% of every $100 spent (up 38% from 2024)
Retail contribution: 10-15% of total revenue for successful medspas
Membership contribution: 20-30% of total revenue
Retention & Visit Frequency:
Members visit 2.9x more annually than non-members
30% higher retention with personalized communication
5% retention increase = 25-95% profit increase

 Average membership length: 38-44 months
Conversion & Upgrade Metrics:
42% of entry-tier members upgrade within 6 months
89% pre-booking rate among members
Members 3.2x more likely to purchase additional services
VIP+ members generate 2.8 referrals/year average

SECTION 3: MEMBERSHIP PSYCHOLOGY {#section-3}
The 7 Behavioral Triggers That Lock in Commitment
1. Sunk Cost Effect
Psychology: Once invested, people justify continued participation Application: Monthly payments create
ongoing psychological investment Design Principle: Automatic recurring billing (never one-time annual only)
2. Loss Aversion
Psychology: Fear of losing benefits outweighs desire to gain new ones Application: "Unused credits expire"
creates urgency to schedule Design Principle: Rolling credits with expiration (2-4 months max)
3. Endowment Effect
Psychology: People value what they "own" more highly Application: Members feel ownership over "their"
credits and benefits Design Principle: Personalized member portals showing "Your Credits" and "Your
Savings"
4. Social Proof & Status
Psychology: Desire to belong to exclusive groups Application: VIP/Elite tier naming, member-only events
Design Principle: Visible status indicators (different colored member cards, priority lanes)
5. Goal Gradient Effect
Psychology: Motivation increases as people approach goals Application: Tiered progression system
encourages upgrades Design Principle: "You're only $X away from Platinum benefits!"
6. Reciprocity Principle
Psychology: People feel obligated to give back when they receive Application: Birthday gifts, surprise
upgrades, free samples Design Principle: Unexpected perks that create "wow" moments

 7. Paradox of Choice
Psychology: Too many options paralyze decisions Application: 3-4 clear tiers (not 7-8 confusing options)
Design Principle: Simple, differentiated value propositions per tier

SECTION 4: THE TIER ARCHITECTURE SYSTEM {#section-4}
The 3-Tier Framework (Scientifically Optimized)
Why 3 Tiers?
Decoy effect: Middle tier appears most valuable
Clear upgrade path without overwhelm
Each tier serves distinct client psychology

TIER 1: THE GATEWAY (Entry)
Price Point: $99-$199/month Target: First-time members, prevention-focused, budget-conscious Psychology:
Lower barrier to entry, taste of membership benefits
Core Structure:
Monthly Credits: $200-$250 in treatment value
Included Services: 1 signature service monthly
Discount Level: 10-15% on additional services
Rollover: Up to 2 months
Retail Discount: 10%

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
                        90-DAY GROWTH PROGRAM
                      TEAM KICKOFF PLAYBOOK
        Your Team's Essential Guide to Implementation Success
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This playbook outlines the critical role your team plays in our 90-day 
transformation program. Inside you'll find your specific action items, timelines, 
and implementation checklist to ensure every team member knows exactly what to 
do and when.

Program Duration: 90 Days
Celebration Event: End of Week 12
Bi-Weekly Check-ins: Every 2 Weeks

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
TABLE OF CONTENTS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

1. Program Overview & Your Role
2. What The Agency Is Handling (Not Your Responsibility)
3. Your Team's Action Items by Week

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1. PROGRAM OVERVIEW & YOUR ROLE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Welcome to your 90-day growth transformation! This program is designed to 
increase your revenue, improve client retention, and create predictable monthly 
income through strategic packages, memberships, and marketing.

YOUR TEAM'S MISSION
-------------------
While our agency handles all advertising, automation, and technical 
implementation, YOUR team is responsible for:

• Collecting creative assets (before/after photos, testimonials, behind-the-
  scenes content)
• Implementing new package offerings and pricing
• Launching and presenting membership tiers to clients
• Enhancing client consultation and sales processes
• Converting leads generated from ads into booked appointments
• Delivering exceptional client experiences that drive retention and referrals
• Planning and executing the 90-day celebration event


═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
2. WHAT THE AGENCY IS HANDLING (NOT YOUR RESPONSIBILITY)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

To keep your team focused on what matters most—client care and sales—our agency 
is managing:

• Running all paid advertising campaigns (Facebook, Instagram, Google)
• Creating ad creative from assets you provide
• Implementing AI-powered follow-up systems
• Building and managing your CRM automation
• Technical campaign optimization and analytics
• Lead tracking and reporting systems

You will NOT need to worry about Facebook Ads Manager, landing page design, 
email sequences, or any technical marketing tasks. That's on us.


═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
3. YOUR TEAM'S ACTION ITEMS BY WEEK
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

WEEK 1-2: FOUNDATION & ASSET COLLECTION
----------------------------------------

CREATIVE ASSETS
• Gather 10-15 before/after photos with signed consent forms
• Record 3-5 video testimonials from happy clients (15-60 seconds)
• Take behind-the-scenes photos of treatment rooms, team, equipment
• Ensure all photos are high resolution (1080p+ for videos)

TEAM REVIEW
• Read package playbook together as a team
• Review membership tier structure
• Identify questions for bi-weekly call

✅ MILESTONE DUE: Creative assets uploaded and ready by end of Week 2


WEEK 3-4: PACKAGE IMPLEMENTATION
---------------------------------

BUILD PACKAGES
• Create 3-5 tiered packages (Foundation, Transformation, Signature)
• Price each package with 45-60% profit margin
• Design package names using aspirational language
• Add packages to booking system and price sheets

PRINT MATERIALS
• Create package menu cards for consultation rooms
• Design package overview brochures
• Update website service menu with packages

✅ MILESTONE DUE: All packages created, priced, and added to booking system by 
   end of Week 4


WEEK 5-6: SALES TRAINING & MEMBERSHIP SETUP
--------------------------------------------

TEAM TRAINING
• Hold team training on package presentation techniques
• Role-play consultation scenarios and objection handling
• Practice explaining value breakdown vs. price
• Train on payment plan presentation

MEMBERSHIP BUILD
• Design 3-tier membership structure (Glow/VIP/Elite)
• Calculate pricing using value equation (2-2.5x perceived value)

4. PACKAGE & UPSELL IMPLEMENTATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This section outlines how to build and present high-value treatment packages.

BUILDING YOUR PACKAGE TIERS
----------------------------

Create 3-5 package tiers following this structure:

┌────────────────┬──────────────┬─────────────────┬─────────────┐
│ TIER           │ PRICE RANGE  │ # OF TREATMENTS │ DURATION    │
├────────────────┼──────────────┼─────────────────┼─────────────┤
│ Foundation     │ $1,200-$2,500│ 3-4 treatments  │ 60-90 days  │
│ Transformation │ $3,500-$7,500│ 6-8 treatments  │ 90-180 days │
│ Signature      │ $8,500-$25K+ │ 12+ treatments  │ 6-12 months │
└────────────────┴──────────────┴─────────────────┴─────────────┘


PACKAGE NAMING STRATEGY
-----------------------

Use aspirational, benefit-focused names instead of generic treatment 
descriptions:

❌ AVOID: "Botox + Filler Package"
✅ USE: "The Executive Refresh - Board Room Ready Protocol"

❌ AVOID: "Summer Body Package"
✅ USE: "The Riviera Transformation - 90-Day Beach Body Blueprint"


PACKAGE COMPONENTS (WHAT TO INCLUDE)
-------------------------------------

Every high-converting package must include:

1. ANCHOR TREATMENT (60% of perceived value)
   The primary modality that addresses the client's chief concern

2. SYNERGISTIC SUPPORT TREATMENTS (30% of perceived value)
   2-3 complementary services that accelerate or enhance results

3. PROFESSIONAL-GRADE PRODUCTS (7% of perceived value)
   Take-home skincare that bridges treatment sessions

4. VIP CONCIERGE ELEMENTS (3% of perceived value)
   Priority booking, dedicated coordinator, complimentary amenities


CONSULTATION PROCESS
--------------------

When presenting packages to clients:

1. Ask open-ended questions to understand their goals
2. Present the package that best matches their desired outcome
3. Show value breakdown: "Individually these services cost $X, but in this 
   package you get them for $Y"
4. Emphasize results and transformation over just services
5. Offer payment plans to make packages accessible
6. Close with urgency: "This Founding Member pricing is only available for the 
   next 30 days"


EXAMPLE PACKAGE: THE EXECUTIVE MOMMY MAKEOVER
----------------------------------------------
Price: $8,999-$14,999
Target: Professional mothers 32-45, household income $200K+

Components:
• 8 sessions EMSculpt Neo (abdomen + flanks)
• 50-100 units neurotoxin (forehead, glabella, crow's feet)
• 2-4 syringes Radiesse or Sculptra (facial volume restoration)
• 6 sessions lymphatic drainage massage
• 4-month GLP-1 peptide therapy protocol
• Professional-grade skincare bundle
• B12 + MIC injections (12 sessions)

Timeline: 6 months with monthly check-ins
Profit Margin: 54-61%
Average Close Rate: 67% when presented to qualified leads

  over $1,800 per year"

6. CLIENT EXPERIENCE ENHANCEMENT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Exceptional client experiences drive retention, referrals, and 5-star reviews.

THE 5-MINUTE RESPONSE RULE
---------------------------

Respond to ALL inquiries within 5 minutes during business hours:

• Phone calls: Answer live or call back immediately
• Web form submissions: Call or text within 5 minutes
• Social media DMs: Respond and move to phone/text
• Email inquiries: Respond same day (faster is better)

WHY IT MATTERS: Leads generated from ads are HOT. The first medspa to respond 
wins 80% of the time.


CONSULTATION BEST PRACTICES
----------------------------

1. Build rapport first - Ask about their day, compliment something genuine

2. Ask diagnostic questions - "What brings you in today?" "What results are you 
   hoping for?"

3. Listen more than you talk - Let them express their concerns fully

4. Educate, don't sell - Explain how treatments work and why they're effective

5. Recommend the best solution - Even if it's a package or membership upgrade

6. Handle objections with empathy - "I understand, many clients felt that way 
   at first..."

7. Close with next steps - Always book the appointment before they leave


COMMON OBJECTIONS & RESPONSES
------------------------------

OBJECTION: "That's too expensive"
RESPONSE: "I totally understand. Let me show you the payment plan options. You 
can break this into 6 monthly payments of $X, which is less than what most 
people spend on coffee each month. And you're investing in yourself—that's 
priceless."

OBJECTION: "I need to think about it"
RESPONSE: "Of course! What specific questions do you have that I can answer for 
you right now? I want to make sure you have all the information you need to 
make the best decision for yourself."

OBJECTION: "I want to check with other medspas first"
RESPONSE: "Smart! You should absolutely do your research. Here's what I can 
tell you: we're offering Founding Member pricing for the next 30 days, so if 
you do decide to move forward with us, booking today locks in this special 
rate. Can I hold a spot for you while you're deciding?"


POST-TREATMENT FOLLOW-UP
-------------------------

Every client should receive:

• 24-hour check-in text: "Hi [Name]! Just checking in—how are you feeling after 
  your treatment yesterday?"

• 48-hour review request: "We'd love to hear about your experience! Would you 
  mind leaving us a quick review? [link]"

• 1-week progress check: "How are you liking your results? Ready to book your 
  next appointment?"

• Before/after photo request: "Your results look amazing! Can we take a quick 
  after photo to show your transformation?"

TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
------------------------

Photos:
• Minimum resolution: 1080p (1920x1080 pixels)
• Preferred formats: JPEG, PNG
• Mix of orientations: Horizontal, vertical, and square
• Natural editing: Minimal filters
• Consistent lighting across all photos

Videos:
• Minimum resolution: 1080p
• Preferred formats: MP4, MOV
• Good natural lighting (avoid harsh shadows)
• Clear audio (no background noise)
• Stable footage (use tripod if possible)


HOW TO GET CLIENT CONSENT
--------------------------

Make it easy and natural:

1. Ask when they're happy with results: "Your transformation is incredible! 
   Would you be comfortable letting us share this to help others?"

2. Offer an incentive: "If you let us use your before/after in marketing, we'll 
   give you 20% off your next treatment"

3. Have consent forms ready to sign immediately

4. Reassure them about their privacy: "We can blur your face or use first name 
   only if you prefer"


CONTENT COLLECTION SCRIPT
--------------------------

"[Client name], your results are absolutely stunning! We love showcasing real 
transformations like yours to help other people see what's possible. Would you 
be willing to let us take a quick after photo and use it in our marketing? 

We'll of course have you sign a consent form, and if you'd prefer we can blur 
your face or just use your first name. As a thank you, I'd love to give you 20% 
off your next treatment.

[If yes] Amazing! Let me grab the consent form and we'll take that photo real 
quick."

4. PACKAGE & UPSELL IMPLEMENTATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This section outlines how to build and present high-value treatment packages.

BUILDING YOUR PACKAGE TIERS
----------------------------

Create 3-5 package tiers following this structure:

┌────────────────┬──────────────┬─────────────────┬─────────────┐
│ TIER           │ PRICE RANGE  │ # OF TREATMENTS │ DURATION    │
├────────────────┼──────────────┼─────────────────┼─────────────┤
│ Foundation     │ $1,200-$2,500│ 3-4 treatments  │ 60-90 days  │
│ Transformation │ $3,500-$7,500│ 6-8 treatments  │ 90-180 days │
│ Signature      │ $8,500-$25K+ │ 12+ treatments  │ 6-12 months │
└────────────────┴──────────────┴─────────────────┴─────────────┘


PACKAGE NAMING STRATEGY
-----------------------

Use aspirational, benefit-focused names instead of generic treatment 
descriptions:

❌ AVOID: "Botox + Filler Package"
✅ USE: "The Executive Refresh - Board Room Ready Protocol"

❌ AVOID: "Summer Body Package"
✅ USE: "The Riviera Transformation - 90-Day Beach Body Blueprint"


PACKAGE COMPONENTS (WHAT TO INCLUDE)
-------------------------------------

Every high-converting package must include:

1. ANCHOR TREATMENT (60% of perceived value)
   The primary modality that addresses the client's chief concern

2. SYNERGISTIC SUPPORT TREATMENTS (30% of perceived value)
   2-3 complementary services that accelerate or enhance results

3. PROFESSIONAL-GRADE PRODUCTS (7% of perceived value)
   Take-home skincare that bridges treatment sessions

4. VIP CONCIERGE ELEMENTS (3% of perceived value)
   Priority booking, dedicated coordinator, complimentary amenities


CONSULTATION PROCESS
--------------------

When presenting packages to clients:

1. Ask open-ended questions to understand their goals
2. Present the package that best matches their desired outcome
3. Show value breakdown: "Individually these services cost $X, but in this 
   package you get them for $Y"
4. Emphasize results and transformation over just services
5. Offer payment plans to make packages accessible
6. Close with urgency: "This Founding Member pricing is only available for the 
   next 30 days"


EXAMPLE PACKAGE: THE EXECUTIVE MOMMY MAKEOVER
----------------------------------------------
Price: $8,999-$14,999
Target: Professional mothers 32-45, household income $200K+

Components:
• 8 sessions EMSculpt Neo (abdomen + flanks)
• 50-100 units neurotoxin (forehead, glabella, crow's feet)
• 2-4 syringes Radiesse or Sculptra (facial volume restoration)
• 6 sessions lymphatic drainage massage
• 4-month GLP-1 peptide therapy protocol
• Professional-grade skincare bundle
• B12 + MIC injections (12 sessions)

Timeline: 6 months with monthly check-ins
Profit Margin: 54-61%
Average Close Rate: 67% when presented to qualified leads

6. CLIENT EXPERIENCE ENHANCEMENT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Exceptional client experiences drive retention, referrals, and 5-star reviews.

THE 5-MINUTE RESPONSE RULE
---------------------------

Respond to ALL inquiries within 5 minutes during business hours:

• Phone calls: Answer live or call back immediately
• Web form submissions: Call or text within 5 minutes
• Social media DMs: Respond and move to phone/text
• Email inquiries: Respond same day (faster is better)

WHY IT MATTERS: Leads generated from ads are HOT. The first medspa to respond 
wins 80% of the time.


CONSULTATION BEST PRACTICES
----------------------------

1. Build rapport first - Ask about their day, compliment something genuine

2. Ask diagnostic questions - "What brings you in today?" "What results are you 
   hoping for?"

3. Listen more than you talk - Let them express their concerns fully

4. Educate, don't sell - Explain how treatments work and why they're effective

5. Recommend the best solution - Even if it's a package or membership upgrade

6. Handle objections with empathy - "I understand, many clients felt that way 
   at first..."

7. Close with next steps - Always book the appointment before they leave


COMMON OBJECTIONS & RESPONSES
------------------------------

OBJECTION: "That's too expensive"
RESPONSE: "I totally understand. Let me show you the payment plan options. You 
can break this into 6 monthly payments of $X, which is less than what most 
people spend on coffee each month. And you're investing in yourself—that's 
priceless."

OBJECTION: "I need to think about it"
RESPONSE: "Of course! What specific questions do you have that I can answer for 
you right now? I want to make sure you have all the information you need to 
make the best decision for yourself."

OBJECTION: "I want to check with other medspas first"
RESPONSE: "Smart! You should absolutely do your research. Here's what I can 
tell you: we're offering Founding Member pricing for the next 30 days, so if 
you do decide to move forward with us, booking today locks in this special 
rate. Can I hold a spot for you while you're deciding?"


POST-TREATMENT FOLLOW-UP
-------------------------

Every client should receive:

• 24-hour check-in text: "Hi [Name]! Just checking in—how are you feeling after 
  your treatment yesterday?"

• 48-hour review request: "We'd love to hear about your experience! Would you 
  mind leaving us a quick review? [link]"

• 1-week progress check: "How are you liking your results? Ready to book your 
  next appointment?"

• Before/after photo request: "Your results look amazing! Can we take a quick 
  after photo to show your transformation?"

TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
------------------------

• Minimum resolution: 1080p (1920x1080 pixels)

1. Ask when they're happy with results: "Your transformation is incredible! 
   Would you be comfortable letting us share this to help others?"

2. Offer an incentive: "If you let us use your before/after in marketing, we'll 
   give you 20% off your next treatment"

3. Have consent forms ready to sign immediately

4. Reassure them about their privacy: "We can blur your face or use first name 
   only if you prefer"

[If yes] Amazing! Let me grab the consent form and we'll take that photo real

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
6. PARTNERSHIP & REFERRAL NETWORK BUILDING
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Strategic partnerships create sustainable client acquisition with ZERO ad spend.

YOUR PARTNERSHIP MISSION
-------------------------

Build 5-10 active partnerships with local businesses that serve your exact 
target client. These partnerships will generate 20-50 new client referrals 
during the 90-day program.

WHY PARTNERSHIPS MATTER
-----------------------

• Zero customer acquisition cost (vs. $50-150 per lead from ads)
• Pre-qualified, warm referrals from trusted sources
• Enhanced local credibility and community presence
• Sustainable long-term growth that compounds over time
• Recession-resistant (referrals continue even when ad budgets shrink)


IDEAL PARTNERSHIP TARGETS
--------------------------

┌──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ BUSINESS TYPE            │ WHY THEY'RE PERFECT                          │
├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Boutique Fitness Studios │ • Shared health-conscious clientele          │
│ (Pilates, Barre, Yoga)   │ • Body confidence focus aligns with your     │
│                          │   aesthetic services                         │
│                          │ • Members visit 3-4x/week = high exposure    │
├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Hair Salons & Stylists   │ • Clients visit every 6-8 weeks              │
│                          │ • Deep trusted relationships                 │
│                          │ • Already discussing beauty and self-care    │
│                          │ • Natural conversation starter               │
├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Luxury Boutiques         │ • Fashion-conscious clients care about       │
│                          │   appearance                                 │
│                          │ • Similar affluent demographic               │
│                          │ • Cross-promotion opportunities              │
├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Real Estate Agents       │ • Need closing gifts for clients             │
│                          │ • Access to affluent homebuyers              │
│                          │ • Wholesale gift certificate opportunity     │
├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Wedding Planners         │ • Bridal clients need pre-wedding treatments │
│                          │ • Built-in timeline (6-12 months)            │
│                          │ • Entire bridal party potential              │
└──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘


THE 5 PARTNERSHIP DEAL STRUCTURES
----------------------------------

Choose the structure that makes sense for each partner:

1. RECIPROCAL REFERRAL
   • Both businesses refer clients to each other (no money exchanged)
   • Example: You refer to their gym, they refer to your medspa
   • Track with unique promo codes
   • Target: 5+ referrals per quarter each direction

2. SERVICE EXCHANGE
   • Trade services at equal value (no cash)
   • Example: $400/month in treatments for their team in exchange for classes
   • Both teams benefit + exposure to each other's clients
   • Promote partnership on social media

3. COMMISSION/KICKBACK
   • Partner receives 10-20% commission for booked referrals
   • Example: Stylist earns 15% of every client they send
   • Paid monthly via Venmo/check
   • Perfect for hair salons, personal trainers

4. CLIENT DISCOUNT
   • Offer partner's clients exclusive discount; they promote you
   • Example: Gym members get "20% off first treatment"
   • Partner promotes via email blast + in-studio signage
   • You provide branded flyers and promo codes

5. GIFT CERTIFICATE PROGRAM
   • Partner includes your voucher in client gifts/welcome packages
   • Example: Real estate agent gives $150 medspa certificate at closing
   • You charge them wholesale ($75 for $150 certificate)
   • 60-70% redemption rate creates new clients


YOUR PARTNERSHIP ACTION ITEMS
------------------------------

WEEK 1-2: PARTNERSHIP RESEARCH
☐ Identify 15-20 potential partner businesses in your area
☐ Research each business (clientele, values, brand positioning)
☐ Prioritize top 10 based on best audience fit
☐ Determine which deal structure fits each partner best

WEEK 3-4: OUTREACH & MEETINGS
☐ Reach out to top 10 partners via email or phone
☐ Schedule coffee/lunch meetings with interested parties
☐ Prepare partnership pitch deck and materials
☐ Conduct 5-7 partnership conversations

WEEK 5-6: PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENTS
☐ Negotiate deal terms with 3-5 partners
☐ Sign partnership agreements (1-page simple contract)
☐ Create promo codes for each partnership
☐ Design promotional materials (flyers, social graphics, referral cards)

WEEK 7-8: PARTNERSHIP LAUNCH
☐ Deliver marketing materials to partners
☐ Train your staff on each partnership and how to track referrals
☐ Launch social media announcements for each partnership
☐ Set up tracking system (spreadsheet or CRM)

WEEK 9-12: ACTIVATION & OPTIMIZATION
☐ Monthly check-ins with each partner
☐ Track referrals and conversion rates
☐ Celebrate wins and send thank-you notes
☐ Optimize underperforming partnerships
☐ Add 2-3 new partnerships if capacity allows


PARTNERSHIP OUTREACH SCRIPT
----------------------------

Use this template to reach out to potential partners:

EMAIL TEMPLATE:

Subject: Partnership opportunity - [Your Medspa] + [Their Business]

Hi [Name],

I'm [Your Name], owner of [Your Medspa]. I've been following [Their Business] 
and am really impressed by [specific compliment about their business].

I think our clients have a lot in common, and I'd love to explore a partnership 
that benefits both of our businesses. I have a few ideas for how we could 
support each other's growth while providing even more value to our clients.

Would you be open to a quick 15-minute coffee chat this week? I promise it'll 
be worth your time 😊

Looking forward to connecting!

[Your Name]
[Your Medspa]
[Phone]


PARTNERSHIP PITCH (IN-PERSON)
------------------------------

When you meet with a potential partner, use this structure:

1. BUILD RAPPORT (2 minutes)
   "Thanks for meeting! I've heard great things about your [studio/salon/etc.]"

2. ESTABLISH COMMON GROUND (3 minutes)
   "I noticed we probably serve a lot of the same clients - women in their 
   30s-50s who care about wellness and self-care..."

3. PRESENT THE OPPORTUNITY (5 minutes)
   "I'd love to create a partnership where we both win. Here's what I'm 
   thinking..."
   [Present specific deal structure]

4. SHOW THE VALUE (3 minutes)
   "For you, this means [their benefit]. For us, this means [your benefit]. 
   For our clients, they get [client benefit]."

5. HANDLE OBJECTIONS (2 minutes)
   "What concerns do you have?"
   [Listen and address]

6. CLOSE WITH NEXT STEPS (2 minutes)
   "Would you be open to trying this for 30 days to see how it goes?"


EXAMPLE PARTNERSHIPS IN ACTION
-------------------------------

PARTNERSHIP #1: HAIR SALON
Deal Structure: Stylist Commission Program
How It Works:
• Individual stylists earn 20% commission on referred clients who book
• Provide each stylist with 50 custom referral cards
• Give them unique promo code (e.g., SARAHSTYLE20)
• Pay commission monthly via Venmo

The Math:
• 5 referrals/month × $300 average spend = $1,500 revenue
• Stylist commission (20%) = $300/month for them
• Your customer acquisition cost = 20% (highly profitable)
• Average stylist earns $3,600/year in extra income


PARTNERSHIP #2: BOUTIQUE FITNESS STUDIO
Deal Structure: Reciprocal Referral + Service Exchange
How It Works:
• You provide $400/month in treatments for studio owner + 2 instructors
• They provide unlimited classes for 3 of your staff members
• Both businesses promote partnership quarterly via email
• Display each other's flyers at reception

Benefits:
• Your team gets fitness classes (great benefit!)
• Their team experiences your treatments (creates advocates)
• Cross-promotion to both email lists
• Zero cash outlay for either business


PARTNERSHIP #3: REAL ESTATE AGENT
Deal Structure: Closing Gift Program
How It Works:
• Agent includes $150 medspa gift certificate in closing gifts
• You charge agent wholesale price ($75 per certificate)
• New client who redeems gets 20% off additional services
• Beautiful branded presentation folder

The Math:
• Agent closes 25 homes/year
• 25 certificates × $75 = $1,875 revenue for you
• 70% redemption = 18 new clients
• Average additional spend on redemption: $300
• 18 clients × $300 = $5,400 additional revenue
• Total partnership value: $7,275/year from one agent


TRACKING YOUR PARTNERSHIPS
---------------------------

Create a simple spreadsheet with these columns:

• Partner Name
• Deal Type
• Start Date
• Promo Code
• Referrals This Month
• Referrals Total
• Revenue Generated
• Status (Active/Paused/Inactive)
• Next Check-in Date

Review monthly and ask:
• Which partnerships are generating the most referrals?
• What's the conversion rate from referral to booked appointment?
• Are we holding up our end of the deal?
• What needs optimization?


90-DAY PARTNERSHIP TARGETS
---------------------------

By the end of 90 days, you should have:

✅ 5-10 signed partnership agreements
✅ 20-50 new client referrals from partners
✅ $3,000-8,000 in revenue from partnership referrals
✅ Established monthly partnership review process
✅ Template and system for adding new partners ongoing
